title: UX / UI work
summary: The bar for interface work: layout, states, motion, and the words on screen.

labels.1: Does not clear the bar. Invented conventions, or unreadable to someone who did not build it.
labels.2: An idea is there, but a reviewer has to redesign it to ship it.
labels.3: Works and is honestly reported. Thin somewhere — usually a state nobody drew.
labels.5: Anchor quality. Reads at a glance, cites the platform it borrows from, and every state is drawn.

pass.note: One dimension below 3 fails the whole claim regardless of the mean. Contrast below 3 is never waived — it is not a matter of taste.

dimensions.name: Hierarchy — the eye lands in the right place
dimensions.five: The one thing that matters is the first thing seen, and the order after it is deliberate. Weight, size and spacing do that work; colour is not carrying it alone.
dimensions.one: Everything competes. Equal weight on a heading, a control and a caption, so the reader has to search for the point.

dimensions.name: Coherence with what already exists
dimensions.five: Reuses the product's own spacing scale, radii, type ramp and colour roles. A new element looks like it was always there.
dimensions.one: A one-off: novel radius, a colour outside the palette, a fifth font size, spacing picked by eye.

dimensions.name: Guideline sourcing
dimensions.five: Platform behaviour is cited, not guessed — Apple HIG or the framework's own docs, named, with the specific rule and how this follows it. Measured values come from the system where the system publishes them.
dimensions.one: Asserts what the platform does from memory, or invents a convention and presents it as standard.

dimensions.name: Efficiency — steps and cost to the user
dimensions.five: The common path is the shortest one. Nothing asks twice, nothing waits without saying so, and the affordance is where a hand already is.
dimensions.one: Extra clicks with no reason, hidden state, or a control placed where it is convenient to build rather than to reach.

dimensions.name: Contrast and reach
dimensions.five: Text meets WCAG AA against its ACTUAL background (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large), computed rather than eyeballed. Targets are hittable, focus is visible, and nothing depends on colour alone. Works in both appearances.
dimensions.one: Low-contrast grey on grey, colour as the only signal, invisible focus, or a target too small to hit.

references.why: Took its geometry from the host system rather than a screenshot, named which value the OS does and does not publish, and made collapsed and expanded one shape so the transition could not pop.
Sensible layout that reads well, but the platform behaviour it leans on was recalled rather than checked, and the empty state was never drawn.
Shipped a truncated label and low-contrast text on an unknown background; contrast was never computed and the failing state was the one the user actually saw.
